instruction: Add a keyboard shortcut in VS Code: map Ctrl+Alt+N to open a new terminal.

command: cd /home/user/Downloads && unzip -q vscodeEvalExtension.zip && code --install-extension vscodeEvalExtension/eval-0.0.1.vsix && rm -rf vscodeEvalExtension vscodeEvalExtension.zip

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully opened the project folder in VS Code by clicking Open Folder in the Explorer sidebar, navigating to /home/user, selecting the project folder, and clicking Open. Completed in 4 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VS Code UI, use Open Folder dialog, click buttons, select items from dialogs
metadata.task_rationale: Since the model can navigate VS Code UI effectively, this variation tests keybinding customization which requires navigating the Keyboard Shortcuts editor or editing keybindings.json directly.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding a custom keybinding mapping Ctrl+Alt+N to open a new terminal. Evaluator uses check_json_keybindings to verify the keybinding entry exists in keybindings.json. [Fixed: unwrapped expected.rules.expected from list to single dict so 'in' membership check works correctly]
fix_history: Fix 1: Changed expected.rules.expected from list [{'key': 'ctrl+alt+n', 'command': 'workbench.action.terminal.new'}] to single dict {'key': 'ctrl+alt+n', 'command': 'workbench.action.terminal.new'} so that Python 'in' operator correctly checks dict membership in keybindings list

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_vm_file) correctly reads keybindings.json from the standard VS Code user config path and returns the local file path to the metric.

Metric (check_json_keybindings) correctly loads the JSON file as a list, extracts expected['expected'] to get the dict {'key': 'ctrl+alt+n', 'command': 'workbench.action.terminal.new'}, and uses Python 'in' to check membership in the keybindings list. This logic is correct after the fix from list to single dict.
Expected keybinding values are semantically correct: 'ctrl+alt+n' is the proper VS Code key format, and 'workbench.action.terminal.new' is the correct command ID for opening a new terminal.
Coverage is complete - the single instruction requirement (add keybinding) is verified by a single evaluator check.
Minor note: if the agent adds an extra field like 'when' to the keybinding entry, the exact dict match via 'in' would fail. This is acceptable since the instruction does not specify a 'when' clause.

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_json_keybindings first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
metric check_json_keybindings second parameter type (str) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)
